questions.question: The most toxic nitrogenous waste excreted by many bony fishes, aquatic amphibians and aquatic insects is:
questions.explanation: Ammonia is the most toxic nitrogenous waste and requires a large amount of water for its elimination. Many bony fishes, aquatic amphibians, and aquatic insects are ammonotelic, meaning they excrete ammonia directly into the surrounding water. Since ammonia is highly water-soluble, it is excreted by diffusion across body surfaces or gill membranes.

questions.explanation: In crustaceans, such as prawns, excretory functions are carried out by antennal glands (also called green glands). These glands help in the removal of nitrogenous wastes and osmoregulation. Both antennal glands and green glands refer to the same excretory structures in crustaceans.

questions.question: Least toxic nitrogenous waste is
questions.explanation: Among nitrogenous wastes, ammonia is the most toxic and requires a large amount of water for excretion, urea is less toxic and needs moderate water, while uric acid is the least toxic and can be excreted with minimal water loss. Uricotelic organisms (birds, reptiles, insects) eliminate uric acid in a solid or paste-like form to conserve water.

questions.question: The kidneys not only remove the waste products from the blood but also play a very important role in maintaining
options: Constant composition of the blood irrespective of the nature of the food or fluid intake
questions.explanation: Explanation: Kidneys play a crucial role in maintaining the constant composition of blood, irrespective of food or fluid intake, through: Osmoregulation: Balancing water and electrolyte levels. Excretion of metabolic wastes like urea, uric acid, and creatinine. Acid-base balance by regulating hydrogen and bicarbonate ions. They also regulate blood pressure through the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) but not constantly.

questions.question: Which of the following structures are situated in the cortical region of the kidney? I. Malpighian corpuscle II. PCT (Proximal Convoluted Tubule) III. DCT (Distal Convoluted Tubule) IV. Loop of Henle V. Collecting duct

Increases permeability of distal convoluted tubule and collecting tubule

questions.question: A decrease in blood pressure/volume will not cause the release of
questions.explanation: Explanation: Renin: Released by Juxtaglomerular cells when blood pressure/volume decreases, triggering the Renin-Angiotensin mechanism to raise blood pressure. Aldosterone: Released as a result of Angiotensin II action, increasing sodium and water reabsorption to raise blood volume and pressure. ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone): Released when blood pressure/volume decreases to promote water reabsorption, increasing blood volume and pressure. Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) is released in response to increased blood pressure/volume, not a decrease. It promotes vasodilation and reduces blood pressure, hence it will not be released when blood pressure/volume decreases.

questions.question: Which one of the following statement is correct with respect to regulation of kidney function?

An increase in glomerular blood flow stimulates formation of Angiotensin II
questions.explanation: Explanation: (A) During summer, water loss through evaporation increases blood osmolarity, stimulating ADH release to conserve water. questions.question: The outline of principal event of urination is given below in unorder manner I. Stretch receptors on the wall of urinary bladder send signal to the CNS II. questions.explanation: Answer: The correct sequence of events in urination (micturition) is: Bladder fills with urine and becomes distended (Step II). Micturition (urination) occurs (Step III). Thus, the correct order is:II → I → IV → III The correct answer is:(A) II → I → IV → III.

hi.question: नीचे दो कथन दिये गये हैंः इनमें से एक अभिकथन A है तथा दूसरा कारण R है। अभिकथन (A): मूत्राशय की दीवारों पर स्थित खिंचाव ग्राही CNS को संकेत भेजते हैं। कारण (R): मूत्र मूत्रवाहिनी में संग्रहीत होता है। ऊपर दिये गये कथनों के प्रकाश में विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन करोः

questions.question: Given below are two statements:Statement I: For micturition, the CNS passes on motor messages to initiate the contraction of smooth muscles of the bladder and simultaneous relaxation of urethral sphincter. Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

hi.explanation: • ग्लोमेरुलर निस्यंदन दर (GFR) में गिरावट रक्तचाप को कम करती है और अभिवाही धमनिका में जक्सटाग्लोमेरुलर (JG) कोशिकाओं द्वारा महसूस की जाती है।• प्रतिक्रिया में, JG कोशिकाएं रेनिन स्रावित करती हैं।• रेनिन रेनिन-एंजियोटेंसिन-एल्डोस्टेरोन प्रणाली (RAAS) शुरू करता है:• एंजियोटेंसिनोजन (यकृत द्वारा उत्पादित) को एंजियोटेंसिन I में परिवर्तित करना।• एंजियोटेंसिन I फिर फेफड़ों में एंजियोटेंसिन-परिवर्तक एंजाइम (ACE) द्वारा एंजियोटेंसिन II में परिवर्तित हो जाता है।• एंजियोटेंसिन II वाहिका-संकुचन द्वारा रक्तचाप बढ़ाता है और सोडियम और जल के पुनरवशोषण के लिए एल्डोस्टेरोन स्राव को उत्तेजित करता है।• (A) एंजियोटेंसिनोजन यकृत द्वारा उत्पादित होता है।• (B) एंजियोटेंसिन I एंजियोटेंसिनोजन पर रेनिन की क्रिया से बनता है।• (D) रेनिन एक एंजाइम है जो पेट में दूध को जमाता है, जो RAAS से असंबंधित है।इसलिए, GFR गिरने पर JG कोशिकाएं रेनिन स्रावित करती हैं।

questions.question: JGA is a special sensitive region formed by cellular modifications in the;

questions.question: Which of the following factors decreases renin secretion? I. Increased BP II. Increased plasma Na+ concentration III. Prostaglandins IV. Angiotensin II

questions.question: Select the correct statements. (C) ANF acts as a check on renin-angiotensin mechanism. → Correct Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) inhibits Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS), lowering blood pressure. (D) ADH causes vasodilation. → Incorrect ADH (Vasopressin) causes vasoconstriction, not vasodilation. (E) Vasopressin is released from adenohypophysis. → Incorrect Vasopressin (ADH) is released from the neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary), not adenohypophysis. Correct Statements: (A), (B), and (C) Thus, the correct answer is:✔ (A) (A), (B) and (C) only.

hi.question: सही कथन चुनें।(A) एंजियोटेन्सिन II अधिवृक्क के वल्कुट को एल्डोस्टेरॉन स्रावित करने के लिए सक्रिय करता है।(B) एल्डोस्टेरॉन से रक्तदाब में वृद्धि होती है।(C) ANF रेनिन-एंजियोटेन्सिन क्रियाविधि पर नियंत्रण के रूप में कार्य करता है।(D) ADH वाहिकाविस्फारण का कारण बनता है।(E) वैसोप्रेसिन एडिनोहाइपोफाइसिस से स्रावित होता है।नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें।

questions.question: Which of the following sequences is correct?
options: An increase in body fluid volume Switch off the osmoreceptors Suppresses the ADH release
ADH Constricting effect on blood vessel B.P. high increased glomerular blood flow increased GFR
Angiotensinogen Angiotensin-I Angiotensin-II Adrenal cortex Aldosterone
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: D. All of these Explanation: Option A: ✅ Correct An increase in body fluid volume leads to a decrease in plasma osmolarity. This switches off the osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus. As a result, the release of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) is suppressed, leading to increased urine production to reduce fluid volume. Option B: ✅ Correct ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone) has a vasoconstrictive effect on blood vessels. This increases blood pressure (B.P.). Higher B.P. results in increased glomerular blood flow in the kidneys. This leads to a higher Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR). Option C: ✅ Correct The Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) follows this sequence: Angiotensinogen (produced by the liver) Renin (released by the kidneys) converts angiotensinogen → Angiotensin-I Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) converts Angiotensin-I → Angiotensin-II Angiotensin-II stimulates the adrenal cortex The adrenal cortex releases Aldosterone, which increases sodium and water retention to increase blood pressure. questions.question: A decrease in blood pressure/volume will not cause the release of
questions.explanation: Explanation: Renin: Released by Juxtaglomerular cells when blood pressure/volume decreases, triggering the Renin-Angiotensin mechanism to raise blood pressure. Aldosterone: Released as a result of Angiotensin II action, increasing sodium and water reabsorption to raise blood volume and pressure. ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone): Released when blood pressure/volume decreases to promote water reabsorption, increasing blood volume and pressure. Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) is released in response to increased blood pressure/volume, not a decrease. It promotes vasodilation and reduces blood pressure, hence it will not be released when blood pressure/volume decreases.

hi.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन वृक्क क्रिया के नियमन में शामिल नहीं है?

questions.question: Which of the following hormones do not lead to the constriction of blood vessels?
questions.explanation: Explanation: Epinephrine: Causes vasoconstriction, increasing blood pressure. Angiotensin II: A potent vasoconstrictor, raising blood pressure. ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone): Also causes vasoconstriction, increasing blood pressure. Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF), however, causes vasodilation (dilation of blood vessels), which reduces blood pressure, making it the only hormone among the options that does not lead to vasoconstriction.

hi.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा हॉर्मोन रक्त वाहिकाओं के संकुचन का कारण नहीं बनता है?
